Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in South Carolina, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Friday, October 23Passed

Your completed application must reach the county voter registration office by 5 p.m. on the 11th day before the election: Friday, October 23, 2026. Because the county first has to mail you the application, if you have not started yet, call or visit your county office now. (official page)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

Your ballot must be received by the county voter registration office by 7 p.m. on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026. The Election Commission suggests mailing it at least one week before Election Day (by Tuesday, October 27). (official page)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Saturday, October 31, 2026. When and where to vote early.

South Carolina’s own page on voting by mail

At school away from home, in South Carolina or in another state? What South Carolina says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

To vote absentee by mail you must fit one of the listed groups: your job, caring for someone sick or disabled, or being held in jail before trial keeps you from voting during all of early voting and on Election Day; you will be away from your county of residence during all of early voting and on Election Day; you have a physical disability; you are 65 or older; you are in the U.S. Armed Forces or Merchant Marine (or their spouse or dependent living with them); or you are admitted to a hospital as an emergency patient on Election Day or in the four days before. Anyone can vote early in person without a reason. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • By mail. Step 1: ask your county voter registration office for an application by phone, in person or by U.S. mail, giving your name, date of birth and the last four digits of your Social Security number; they mail you an application. Step 2: fill it out, sign it and return it by U.S. mail or by hand to the county office. State law no longer allows applications by email, fax or online. (official page)
  • In person. You can visit your county voter registration office to ask for and return the application. A close family member (spouse, parent, child, brother, sister, grandparent, grandchild or in-law), or an authorized representative for a voter who is ill or disabled, may ask for and hand in an application for you; they must hand it in in person, not by mail. (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it to your county voter registration office in time to arrive by 7 p.m. on Election Day. (official page)
  • In person. Hand it in at your county voter registration office or an early voting center, and show a photo ID. A close family member or authorized representative may hand it in for you in person (not by mail) if you both fill out and sign the Authorized Returnee form and they show photo ID; one person may return no more than five ballots besides their own. (official page)

What the envelope needs

Sign the voter's oath on the return envelope and have your signature witnessed by anyone 18 or older; a notary is not needed. Put the ballot in the "ballot herein" envelope, then in the return envelope. If you hand in the ballot in person, you must show a photo ID (a driver's license, another state DMV photo ID, a passport, a military photo ID, or a South Carolina voter card with photo). (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on South Carolina’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Monday, October 19, 2026 to Saturday, October 31, 2026.

Early voting runs Monday, October 19 through Saturday, October 31, 2026, 8:30 a.m. to 6 p.m. Monday through Saturday (closed Sunday, October 25), at any early voting center in your county. Bring a photo ID. No reason is needed. (official page)

Students

At school in South Carolina, away from home

The Election Commission says students can register where they live while at college (for example a dorm) or at a South Carolina address they mean to return to (for example the family home); it is up to you, but you can choose only one. If you are registered at home and go to school far away, you may qualify to vote absentee by mail if you will be away from your home county during all of early voting and on Election Day. If you are registered at your college address, you can vote early or on Election Day in that county. (official page)

At school in another state, with South Carolina as home

The Election Commission's student page does not speak separately to South Carolina students at school in another state. The general rule for an absentee ballot is that you will be away from your county of residence during all of early voting and on Election Day. The page says students registered in another state should follow that state's rules (it points to the U.S. Election Assistance Commission at eac.gov). (official page)

Military and overseas

Military and overseas voters use the Federal Post Card Application to register and to be listed as military or overseas voters. Those who choose email get their ballot by email at least 45 days before the election. For November 3, 2026, the federal guide says the ballot request must be received by Election Day; a ballot returned by email or fax must arrive by 7 p.m. on Election Day, and a mailed ballot must be sent by 7 p.m. on Election Day and arrive by 5 p.m. on Thursday, November 5. A Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot from FVAP.gov is also accepted. (federal guide)

South Carolina in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • The application deadline is close: 5 p.m. Friday, October 23, 2026, and applications cannot be sent by email, fax or online. Voters who can get to an early voting center (through Saturday, October 31) do not need a reason.
  • The Federal Voting Assistance Program's state guide was read through the content feed its own page loads.
